name: August Storck
desc: Berlin-based family confectionery maker, Germany's second-largest sweets producer, with brands such as Knoppers and Dickmann's.
capacity_detail: Revenue of USD 2bn in 2025, ranked 17th among global confectionery makers
markets: Sells confectionery through country subsidiaries worldwide from its Berlin parent; ranked 13th largest confectionery producer globally in 2022.
rationale: Mass-market chocolate and candy brands need global reach; F1's broad family audience suits impulse snack brands like Knoppers.

name: Dussmann Group
desc: Berlin-based services group providing facility management, technical building services, senior care and the Dussmann KulturKaufhaus.
markets: Operates with almost 72,000 employees in 23 countries, including Germany and Italy.
rationale: B2B services brand seeking corporate clients could use F1 hospitality to reach facility and real-estate decision makers.

name: Haribo
desc: Family-owned German maker of gummy bears and other sweets, produced in Germany and across European plants.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2,889m in DDW ranking of Rhineland-Palatinate's largest family companies
markets: Produces in four German plants and ten others in Europe; products sold in more than one hundred countries.
rationale: Globally recognised family brand with a young audience; F1's growth among younger fans fits Haribo's mass-market sweets.

name: Rotkäppchen-Mumm
desc: Germany's leading sparkling wine group, owning Rotkäppchen and Mumm Sekt brands plus spirits and wines.
markets: Sites in several German states and in Veneto, Italy; brands sold mainly in Germany and Europe.
rationale: Sparkling wine is tied to podium celebrations; a German sekt group could use F1 hospitality and celebration moments.

name: Biotronik
desc: Berlin family company making pacemakers, defibrillators and cardiac monitoring devices sold in over 100 countries.
markets: Research and production in Europe, the USA and Singapore; sells in more than 100 countries.
rationale: Precision engineering and telemetry story parallels F1 technology; B2B hospitality could reach hospital and cardiology customers.

name: Max Bögl
desc: Family-owned construction group building infrastructure, precast concrete, wind turbine towers and maglev transport systems.
markets: Seven precast plants and over 30 further locations in Germany and other European countries.
rationale: Engineering-led builder with export ambitions in transport tech could use F1 to showcase innovation to infrastructure clients.

name: EW Group
desc: Wesjohann family holding of over 300 companies in poultry, fish and plant breeding, including Aviagen.
markets: Holding of more than 300 companies operating worldwide; Aviagen alone runs 500 sites globally.
rationale: Mostly B2B genetics firm; limited consumer brand need makes F1 a long shot beyond corporate hospitality.

name: PHW-Gruppe (Wiesenhof)
desc: Germany's largest poultry company, selling chicken, turkey and duck products under the Wiesenhof brand.
markets: Largest poultry business in Germany and fourth-largest in Europe; Wiesenhof brand sold mainly in Germany.
rationale: Consumer food brand with heavy German retail presence; F1 activations could support Wiesenhof brand and protein-snack launches.

name: Krone Group
desc: Family-owned maker of forage harvesting machinery and commercial vehicle trailers, headquartered in Emsland.
markets: Production in Germany and Turkey with foreign sales companies for trailers and agricultural machinery.
rationale: Engineering brand selling to farmers and fleets; F1 B2B hospitality could support dealer and fleet relationships.

name: Hubert Burda Media
desc: Family-owned German media group publishing magazines and running digital businesses across 18 countries.
markets: Around 500 media products published in 18 countries, with foreign subsidiaries.
rationale: Media group could pair F1 content partnerships with its lifestyle and car titles to grow advertising audiences.

name: ebm-papst
desc: German manufacturer of electric motors and ventilation fans, agreed to be sold to Madison Air in 2026.
capacity_detail: Agreed sale to Madison Air for EUR 4.775bn announced August 2026
markets: Global maker of fans and motors with plants and sales units in many countries; sales led from Mulfingen.
rationale: Air-movement and efficiency engineering echoes F1 aerodynamics and cooling; new owner may invest in brand building.

name: Leonhard Weiss
desc: Family-owned construction company active in rail track building, road construction, civil engineering and turnkey building.
markets: Construction work in Germany and other European countries from Göppingen and Satteldorf.
rationale: Mainly domestic B2B contractor; F1 has limited fit beyond regional hospitality; at most an option for corporate hospitality with construction contractor customers at European races.

name: SICK
desc: Unlisted family-controlled maker of sensors for factory, logistics and process automation, employing about 11,800 people.
sponsorships: Naming sponsor of Messe Freiburg hall (Sick-Arena)
markets: Worldwide sensor maker for factory, logistics and automation markets.
rationale: Sensor and lidar technology parallels F1 data acquisition; a technical partnership could showcase its automation sensors.

name: Haniel
desc: Duisburg-based family holding owning businesses such as hygiene services, packaging machinery and textiles.
markets: Portfolio companies operate in Germany and many other countries.
rationale: Holding company itself has little brand need; portfolio firms might use F1 for B2B reach.

name: Zwilling J. A. Henckels
desc: Solingen maker of kitchen knives, scissors, cookware and cutlery, owned by the Werhahn group since 1970.
markets: Premium knives and cookware sold worldwide under the Zwilling brand.
rationale: Premium German kitchen brand with global retail presence; F1 precision and craftsmanship stories suit chef-knife marketing.

name: Fressnapf
desc: European pet supplies retail chain with franchise stores, operating as Fressnapf and Maxi Zoo.
ownership: founder-owned (majority via Allegro Invest; Cinven minority)
markets: Pet stores across Germany and other European countries under Fressnapf and Maxi Zoo.
rationale: Pan-European consumer retailer could use F1's European races for broad brand awareness.

name: Aunde Group
desc: Automotive supplier making seat covers, technical textiles, springs, complete seats and interior parts.
markets: Supplies carmakers internationally under the Aunde, Isringhausen and Fehrer brands.
rationale: Automotive interior supplier could use F1 technical partnership to court carmaker customers.

name: Vorwerk
desc: Family-owned Wuppertal group selling Thermomix kitchen appliances and Kobold vacuum cleaners through direct sales.
markets: Direct sales of Thermomix and Kobold appliances in many countries.
rationale: Thermomix is a premium global appliance brand; F1 lifestyle content could broaden reach beyond direct-sales networks.

name: Phoenix Contact
desc: Family-owned maker of electrical connectors, industrial automation and charging technology, based in Blomberg.
sponsorships: Main sponsor of Formula Student car OWL 2.2 (2023)
markets: Global electrical connection and automation supplier with subsidiaries worldwide.
rationale: Already backs Formula Student; e-mobility charging and automation tech could link to F1 engineering and electrification.

name: Mubea
desc: Family-owned lightweight components specialist for cars, aerospace and micromobility, including carbon specialist Carbo Tech.
markets: Supplies automotive and aerospace customers worldwide, from headquarters in Attendorn, Germany.
rationale: Owns Carbo Tech, a racing composites maker; lightweight engineering fits naturally with F1 technical partnerships.

name: Neumann Kaffee Gruppe
desc: Privately held Hamburg group trading and processing green coffee, with farms, mills and export businesses worldwide.
markets: More than 40 companies in 28 countries along the coffee supply chain, from origin farms to import markets.
rationale: Largely B2B commodity trader; F1 fit limited to corporate hospitality with roasters and retailers.

name: Bauer Media Group
desc: Family-owned Hamburg publisher of TV-listing and women's magazines and owner of European radio stations.
markets: Main foreign markets include Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, the UK, Ireland and other European countries.
rationale: Radio and magazine group could build F1 content and audio partnerships across its UK and European stations.

name: Döhler
desc: Family-owned Darmstadt maker of natural flavours, colours and ingredient systems for food and beverage producers.
markets: Subsidiaries and plants in India, Poland, China, Brazil, Dubai, Mexico and many other countries.
rationale: B2B ingredients supplier to drinks brands; F1 hospitality could deepen ties with beverage customers already in motorsport.

name: Deutsche Vermögensberatung (DVAG)
desc: Frankfurt financial advisory company selling insurance, savings and investment products through thousands of independent advisers.
markets: Advisory offices across Germany, with partner companies in Austria.
rationale: Brand-led financial adviser targeting broad German audiences; motorsport sponsorship could support adviser recruitment and awareness.

name: Schütz
desc: Family-owned maker of industrial packaging such as IBC containers and drums, plus energy and foam products.
markets: Industrial packaging production and service network serving chemical and food customers internationally.
rationale: Industrial B2B supplier; F1 offers limited consumer value but some customer hospitality potential.

name: Renolit
desc: Family-owned Worms producer of high-quality plastic films and related products for industrial and building uses.
markets: Active on four continents in 20 countries with more than 30 production and sales companies.
rationale: Materials company; F1 interest mainly as technical supplier for films and wraps.

name: Possehl Group
desc: Lübeck technology group with over 200 companies in printing, precious metals, automotive and other industries.
markets: More than 200 companies in over 30 countries.
rationale: Diversified B2B holding; limited brand need, though portfolio firms serve automotive customers.

name: Bartels-Langness (Bela)
desc: Kiel food wholesaler operating famila hypermarkets, cash-and-carry stores and supply to independent retailers in northern Germany.
markets: Wholesale and famila hypermarkets in northern Germany, including Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg and Lower Saxony.
rationale: Domestic grocery retailer; F1 has low relevance outside promotions with drinks partners.

name: engelbert strauss
desc: Family-run workwear brand selling clothing and safety footwear online and via its own workwear stores.
sponsorships: Sponsor of Liverpool FC and Los Angeles FC (2024); MLB workwear partner and helmet sponsor (from Oct 2024); German national football team; Eintracht Frankfurt
markets: Sells online and through stores in Germany, opened a store in Los Angeles; sponsorships in UK and US.
rationale: Already spends on Premier League and MLB sponsorships; F1 pit-crew workwear tie-in would fit its global expansion.

name: Thalia
desc: German bookstore chain selling books online and in stores across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
ownership: private: Herder family, Leif Erik Göritz and management
markets: Bookstores in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, where branches carry the Orell Füssli brand.
rationale: Book retailer with little motorsport link; F1 publishing tie-ins possible but marginal.

name: Breuninger
industry: luxury department store and online fashion
desc: Stuttgart premium department store chain and online fashion retailer owned by three families.
markets: Department stores in German cities and online fashion sales across Europe.
rationale: Premium fashion retailer whose affluent customers overlap F1's luxury audience; hospitality and collaborations possible.

name: Dallmayr
desc: Family-owned Munich coffee roaster, delicatessen and one of Europe's leading vending machine operators.
markets: Roasts coffee at five German sites and runs over 100,000 vending machines in Europe.
rationale: Premium coffee brand with vending and hospitality business; F1 paddock coffee or hospitality partnership is plausible.

name: Pfeifer & Langen
desc: Cologne food group producing sugar under the Diamant brand, with snack maker Intersnack as group company.
markets: Sugar factories in Germany and other European countries.
rationale: Sugar is a commodity business; F1 relevance comes only through consumer brands such as Intersnack.

name: Häfele
desc: Family-owned supplier of furniture fittings, architectural hardware and electronic locking systems to over 150 countries.
markets: 52 sales subsidiaries worldwide, delivering to 150 countries and more than 160,000 customers.
rationale: Global B2B brand serving architects and joiners; F1 hospitality and hospitality-sector projects could raise profile.

name: Lapp Group
desc: Family-owned Stuttgart maker of cables and connection systems, with 26 production sites and presence in 80 countries.
markets: Manufactures at 26 international sites and is active in over 80 countries.
rationale: Cable and connectivity brand (ÖLFLEX) could showcase reliability in F1 garages and factories as a technical supplier.

name: Motel One
desc: Munich-based budget design hotel group with 109 hotels and about 30,000 rooms in 13 countries.
ownership: private equity: PAI Partners (80% of operations, announced Mar 2025)
markets: 109 hotels in 13 countries, mainly European city centres (August 2026).
rationale: Design-led hotel brand expanding across European cities; F1 race-weekend hospitality and city races fit its traveller base.

name: Vector Informatik
desc: Stuttgart developer of software tools and embedded components for networked vehicle electronics, owned by foundations.
ownership: foundation-owned: Vector Stiftung and a family foundation
markets: 33 locations including the UK, India and China; components used in nearly all networked cars worldwide.
rationale: Automotive electronics tools are used across motorsport engineering; F1 technical partnership would reinforce its engineering brand.

name: Wanzl
desc: Family-owned maker of shopping trolleys, airport luggage carts, retail shelving and self-service checkout systems.
markets: Service and sales subsidiaries worldwide; trolleys exported across Europe and beyond, including US airports.
rationale: Mainly a shopping trolleys and retail fixtures business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: Simba Dickie Group
desc: Family-owned Fürth toy group combining Simba Toys, Dickie Toys, Majorette, Smoby and Schuco model vehicles.
markets: Production in Europe and Asia with a worldwide distribution network.
rationale: Toy-car and model-vehicle brands such as Majorette and Schuco suit F1 licensing and fan-merchandise partnerships.

name: Kostal
desc: Family-owned Lüdenscheid developer of electronic and mechatronic products, mainly for the automotive industry.
markets: Production and subsidiaries in Ireland, the UK, Japan, China, France and other countries.
rationale: Automotive electronics and charging supplier could use F1 to strengthen ties with carmakers and e-mobility customers.

name: Otto Fuchs Group
desc: Family-owned metal processor forging wheels and aerospace parts, and parent of window and facade maker Schüco.
capacity_detail: Group revenue EUR 3.4bn in 2024, including Schüco
markets: Forging plants and subsidiaries including Weber Metals (USA) and a South African unit; Schüco sells internationally.
rationale: Forged lightweight wheels and aerospace alloys suit F1 engineering stories; Schüco brand could add B2B hospitality.

name: Katjes
desc: German maker of fruit gums and liquorice sweets, owned 90% by Bastian Fassin.
markets: Sold mainly in Germany, with a separate international sister company, Katjes International.
rationale: Domestic sweets brand; F1 is a stretch except through German race promotions.

name: Maritim Hotels
desc: German hotel chain running 24 Maritim hotels at home and ten more in seven other countries.
markets: 24 hotels in Germany and 10 hotels in seven other countries, including Egypt.
rationale: Conference-hotel brand could use F1 hospitality, but limited international footprint; at most an option for corporate hospitality with hotel chain customers at European races.

name: Flyeralarm
desc: Würzburg online printer producing flyers, marketing materials and merchandise for businesses across Europe.
markets: Branches in twelve other European countries; production at 15 sites in Germany.
rationale: Has used sports naming rights before; F1 merchandise printing and SME marketing could follow.

name: Beurer
desc: Family-owned Ulm company making blood pressure monitors, scales, heating pads and personal care electrical devices.
markets: Active in 140 countries, with production in Hungary.
rationale: Consumer health brand active in 140 countries; F1 performance and wellbeing themes could support its fitness devices.

name: Duravit
desc: Black Forest manufacturer of designer ceramic sanitaryware, bathroom furniture and wellness products, owned by the Greinert family.
sponsorships: Sponsor of amateur and professional sport (unspecified)
markets: Sells design bathroom products internationally from German and foreign plants.
rationale: Premium design brand; F1 hospitality suites and luxury real estate customers offer modest fit.

name: Röhlig Logistics
desc: Owner-managed Bremen freight forwarder for intercontinental sea and air cargo with over 150 offices.
markets: Over 150 own offices in more than 35 countries, including Mexico, the USA, India and Belgium.
rationale: Freight forwarders such as DHL and DP World back F1; Röhlig could seek visibility with shippers via motorsport logistics.

name: Erbe Elektromedizin
desc: Family-led Tübingen maker of electrosurgical instruments and devices, with 21 subsidiaries worldwide.
markets: Subsidiaries in Europe, China, India, Brazil, Singapore and others; dealers cover 140 further countries.
rationale: Specialist B2B medical brand; F1 relevance is low; at most an option for corporate hospitality with electrosurgical equipment customers at European races.

name: Hansa-Flex
desc: Unlisted Bremen hydraulics company producing hoses and components with 471 branches in 43 countries.
markets: 471 branches in 43 countries in 2025, 193 of them in Germany.
rationale: Industrial service brand; F1 fit limited to B2B hospitality; at most an option for corporate hospitality with hydraulic components and services customers at European races.

name: Bahlsen
desc: Family-owned Hanover maker of biscuits and baked snacks, best known for its Leibniz butter biscuits.
markets: Sales companies across Europe; plants in Germany and Poland.
rationale: Snack brand with European reach; F1 could support snacking campaigns, but budget fit is uncertain.

name: Krombacher
desc: Family-owned brewery and one of Germany's largest, producing Krombacher Pils and non-alcoholic beers.
sponsorships: Sponsor of esports organisation SK Gaming (from Aug 2020); sponsor in several sports
markets: Sold mainly in Germany; 5.74 million hectolitres sold in Germany in 2023.
rationale: Big German sports sponsor; F1 alcohol-free beer activations mirror rivals Heineken and Estrella Galicia 0,0.

name: Warsteiner
desc: Family-owned Sauerland brewery group producing Warsteiner beer, exported to more than 60 countries.
markets: Warsteiner exported to more than 60 countries; breweries in Warstein and Bavaria.
rationale: Exporting beer brand in over 60 countries; F1 alcohol-free beer category could support its international push.

name: Zentis
desc: Family-owned Aachen producer of jams, fruit preparations for dairy makers and sweets such as marzipan.
sponsorships: Partner of Alemannia Aachen (shirt sponsor 1992-1997, partner again since 2022)
markets: Production sites in Germany and abroad supplying dairy and retail customers.
rationale: Mostly B2B ingredient business with a domestic retail brand; F1 relevance is low.

name: Hochland
desc: Family-owned Allgäu cheese maker producing processed and sliced cheese brands including Grünländer.
markets: Plants in Germany, France, Spain, Poland and other countries, plus a large Russian business.
rationale: Mass-market food brand; F1 is plausible for European awareness but its Russian exposure may complicate partnerships.

name: Tchibo
desc: Hamburg coffee roaster and retailer selling coffee and weekly-changing consumer goods in stores and online.
markets: Sells in Germany and other European markets through Tchibo International; 10,708 employees worldwide in 2023.
rationale: Major German coffee brand; F1 hospitality coffee and consumer promotions could help it compete with rivals' sports spends.

name: Hassia Mineralquellen
desc: Family-owned Bad Vilbel bottler and Germany's second-largest branded mineral water company after Gerolsteiner.
markets: Bottles and sells mineral waters and soft drinks mainly in Germany, including eastern states.
rationale: Mainly a mineral water and soft drinks business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: Dr. Wolff Group (Alpecin)
desc: Bielefeld maker of hair and skin care brands including Alpecin caffeine shampoo, Alcina, Linola and Vagisan.
sponsorships: Naming sponsor of Alpecin cycling teams (since 2014; Alpecin-Premier Tech from 2026); partner of Arminia Bielefeld
markets: Sells in Germany and growing in other countries; cycling sponsorship gives international visibility.
rationale: Already a big sports naming sponsor; Alpecin's male, performance-oriented brand fits F1's audience well.

name: Schwan-Stabilo
desc: Family-owned group making Stabilo pens, contract cosmetic pencils and Deuter rucksacks, with 38 sites worldwide.
markets: 38 sites in 27 countries across Europe, North and South America and Asia.
rationale: Stabilo is a consumer brand with global school reach; F1 offers modest fit through youth engagement programmes.

name: KOMSA
desc: Saxony-based distributor and service provider for mobile devices, IT and telecommunications products.
markets: Distribution and services mainly for German telecom and IT retail markets.
rationale: B2B distributor; F1 has little relevance beyond partner hospitality; at most an option for corporate hospitality with telecom and IT distribution customers at European races.

name: Veltins
desc: Sauerland brewery producing Veltins Pilsener and mixed beer drinks, solely owned by Susanne Veltins.
sponsorships: Former main and shirt sponsor of FC Schalke 04 (1997-2001); sponsor of various sports
markets: Beer sold mainly in Germany, from headquarters in Meschede-Grevenstein, Germany.
rationale: Heavy sports sponsor in Germany; alcohol-free beer could follow Heineken's and Paulaner's F1 playbook at German races.

name: HiPP
desc: Family-owned organic baby food and baby care maker, with group seat in Sachseln and German base in Pfaffenhofen.
capacity_detail: Revenue CHF 1,050m (EUR 1,133m) in the D&B/Handelszeitung Top 500 ranking (2022)
markets: Baby food sold in Germany, Switzerland and other European markets.
rationale: Baby food is a poor fit with F1's audience and alcohol/gambling-heavy sponsor mix.

name: Ehrmann
desc: Family-owned Bavarian dairy making yoghurts, quark and desserts sold in more than 50 countries.
sponsorships: Former main sponsor of SC Freiburg (2010/11-2015/16)
markets: Products sold in over 50 countries; two Russian subsidiaries.
rationale: Protein-dessert brands target active consumers; Bundesliga sponsorship history shows appetite for sport, though Russian exposure is a risk.

name: Teekanne
desc: Family-owned Düsseldorf tea company that pioneered branded packaged tea blends and produces internationally.
markets: Production sites and branches in several countries; about 1,200 employees in 2023.
rationale: Tea brand with modest marketing budgets; F1 fit is weak; at most an option for corporate hospitality with tea company customers at European races.

name: Ritter Sport
desc: Family-owned Waldenbuch chocolate maker producing square Ritter Sport bars, present in more than 100 countries.
markets: Present in more than 100 countries; subsidiaries in the UK, Italy, Austria, Singapore and others.
rationale: Iconic German consumer brand growing abroad; F1 offers global visibility comparable to rivals' sports sponsorships.

name: Develey
desc: Family-owned Munich-area producer of mustard, ketchup and sauces, with plants across Europe and Turkey.
markets: Production in Germany, France, Poland, Austria, Slovakia, Czechia, Turkey and Russia.
rationale: Condiments brand; F1 relevance mainly via hospitality catering supply; at most an option for corporate hospitality with condiments maker customers at European races.

name: Helu Kabel
desc: Family-owned producer and distributor of cables, wires and cable accessories with 76 sites in 43 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 796.2m (latest reported); nearly EUR 1.1bn in 2023
markets: 76 locations in 43 countries, including Austria, Mexico, Brazil and Morocco.
rationale: Mainly a cables and wires business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: s.Oliver
desc: German fashion company selling s.Oliver and comma clothing through stores, wholesale and online in about 20 countries.
sponsorships: Sports sponsor since the 1990s; Basketball Bundesliga league sponsor 2000-2003
markets: Products offered in about 20 countries, including Austria, Switzerland, Benelux, Italy, Spain and Canada.
rationale: Mass-fashion brand with sports sponsorship history; F1 lifestyle capsule collections could support international growth.

name: Festool
desc: German maker of premium power tools for tradespeople, exporting 76% of output to 68 countries.
markets: Present in 68 countries with subsidiaries in 25 countries; 76% export share.
rationale: Premium tool brand competing with DeWalt, an F1 partner; pit-garage tool partnership is a natural fit.

name: nobilia
desc: Germany-based maker of fitted kitchens and Europe's market leader in kitchen furniture, exporting to about 90 countries.
markets: 54% of production exported to around 90 countries, with France a key market.
rationale: Mass kitchen brand selling through retailers; F1 exposure could build consumer brand awareness in export markets.

name: Häcker Küchen
desc: One of Germany's largest kitchen manufacturers, owned by the Finkemeier family, with 40% export share.
markets: Exports about 40% of output, from headquarters in Rödinghausen, Germany.
rationale: Kitchen brand; F1 relevance limited to premium-kitchen marketing; at most an option for corporate hospitality with fitted kitchen manufacturer customers at European races.

name: hagebau
industry: building materials and DIY retail network
desc: Network of about 350 independent building-materials and DIY retailers trading jointly under the hagebau brand.
markets: Member businesses in Germany and neighbouring countries; logistics centres across Germany.
rationale: DIY retail network with tool-buying customers; F1 promotions could support private-label and partner brands.

name: Thomann
desc: Family-owned online and store retailer of musical instruments, the world's highest-revenue music retailer.
markets: Delivered to customers in 120 countries in 2024.
rationale: Online retailer with global customers; F1 reach is broad but fit with music gear is limited.

name: Conrad Electronic
desc: Family-owned electronics retailer and B2B sourcing platform for technical products, active in 17 European countries.
markets: Active in 17 European countries via international group companies.
rationale: Technical products retailer targeting engineers and makers; F1 engineering content could suit B2B marketing.

name: notebooksbilliger.de
desc: German online retailer of notebooks, computers and consumer electronics, with additional physical stores.
sponsorships: Sponsored a team in the Carrera Panamericana with Jochen Mass (2011)
markets: Sells mainly to German consumers online and through stores.
rationale: Mainly a online electronics retailer business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: DATEV
desc: Nuremberg software co-operative providing accounting, tax and payroll software to tax advisers and their clients.
sponsorships: Title sponsor of triathlon Challenge Roth since 2013
markets: Germany plus Czechia, Slovakia, Austria, Italy, Poland, Spain and Hungary.
rationale: Already a long-term endurance-sport sponsor; F1 is a big step but could raise brand among business owners.

name: Ravensburger
desc: Ravensburg maker of board games, jigsaw puzzles and children's books, exporting to more than fifty countries.
markets: Products exported to more than fifty countries, from headquarters in Ravensburg, Germany.
rationale: Puzzles and games licensing with F1 teams or tracks could reach family fans.

name: Playmobil (Horst Brandstätter Group)
desc: Foundation-owned toy group behind Playmobil figures and play sets, sold across Europe and North America.
markets: Sales units in many European countries and in the USA, Canada and Mexico.
rationale: Playmobil racing sets and licensed F1 toys could connect with young fans.

name: Viega
desc: Family-owned Attendorn maker of pipe fittings, press connection and installation systems for buildings.
markets: Sells installation technology internationally with plants in Germany and abroad.
rationale: Mainly a plumbing and installation systems business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: Werhahn
desc: Neuss family conglomerate active in building materials, consumer goods such as Zwilling, and financial services.
markets: Group companies operate in Germany and internationally, from headquarters in Neuss, Germany.
rationale: Holding company; any F1 interest would come via consumer brands like Zwilling.

name: GMH Gruppe (Georgsmarienhütte)
desc: Steel group around the Georgsmarienhütte electric steel plant, controlled by Jürgen Großmann since 1993.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,900m in DDW ranking of Hamburg's largest family companies
markets: Steel and forging plants mainly in Germany serving mobility, energy and machinery customers.
rationale: Industrial steelmaker; F1 relevance low; at most an option for corporate hospitality with steel and metal processing group customers at European races.

name: Rolex
desc: Geneva luxury watch manufacturer, owner of Tudor, wholly controlled by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.
capacity_detail: Revenue CHF 4,800m (EUR 5,180m) in the D&B/Handelszeitung Top 500 ranking (2022)
markets: Luxury watches sold worldwide through authorised retailers; owns retailer Bucherer.
rationale: Top luxury sports sponsor whose rivals TAG Heuer, Richard Mille and Breitling are F1 partners; F1 return is plausible.

name: Bühler Group
desc: Family-owned Swiss technology group known for grain milling and food processing equipment and other industrial technologies.
markets: Internationally active technology group serving food and materials processors worldwide.
rationale: Industrial technology group; F1 B2B hospitality could support relationships with large food and industrial customers.

name: Octapharma
desc: Owner-managed Swiss producer of human plasma-based medicines, with products used in over 118 countries.
markets: Over 9,000 employees in 31 branches in 2020; medicines used in more than 118 countries.
rationale: Pharma company with limited consumer brand need; F1 relevance low; at most an option for corporate hospitality with plasma-derived medicines customers at European races.

name: Hamilton
desc: Family-owned Swiss maker of medical technology, sensors, laboratory automation and storage systems.
capacity_detail: Revenue CHF 650m (EUR 701m) in the D&B/Handelszeitung Top 500 ranking (2022)
markets: Operations in Switzerland, with sites and sales internationally.
rationale: Mainly a laboratory automation and medical ventilators business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: Ringier
desc: Family-owned Swiss media group with print, digital, TV and radio brands and online marketplaces.
markets: Media brands in print, digital, TV and radio, plus marketplaces, in Switzerland and other countries.
rationale: Mainly a media and digital marketplaces group business with limited brand need; F1 fit is corporate hospitality at most.

name: Triumph International
desc: International underwear and lingerie maker founded in Heubach, wholly owned by the Braun and Spiesshofer families.
markets: Sells underwear and lingerie internationally, from headquarters in Bad Zurzach, Switzerland.
rationale: Lingerie brand has little natural link to F1; at most an option for corporate hospitality with lingerie and underwear maker customers at European races.

name: Metrohm
desc: Swiss maker of titration, spectroscopy and ion chromatography instruments, wholly owned by the Metrohm Foundation.
markets: Analytical instruments sold worldwide, from headquarters in Herisau, Switzerland.
rationale: Lab-instrument brand; F1 relevance limited to fuel and lubricant testing stories; at most an option for corporate hospitality with analytical instruments customers at European races.

name: Oettinger Davidoff
desc: Family-owned Basel tobacco group making Davidoff, Camacho and other premium cigars.
markets: Premium cigars sold internationally; operations in Honduras and Miami.
rationale: Tobacco advertising is banned in F1; Davidoff could only appear via non-tobacco lifestyle products.

name: Bertschi
desc: Family-owned logistics company transporting liquid and bulk products for the chemical industry, present in 38 countries.
markets: Present in 38 countries worldwide, from headquarters in Dürrenäsch, Switzerland.
rationale: B2B chemical logistics; low F1 relevance; at most an option for corporate hospitality with chemical logistics customers at European races.

name: Planzer
desc: Family-owned Swiss transport, warehouse logistics and parcel company with over 5,600 employees.
markets: Transport, warehousing and parcel services mainly in Switzerland.
rationale: Domestic logistics brand; low F1 relevance; at most an option for corporate hospitality with transport, warehousing and parcels customers at European races.

name: Galliker Transport
desc: Family-owned Swiss transport and logistics company active internationally, wholly owned by the Galliker family.
markets: Transport and logistics in Switzerland and across Europe.
rationale: B2B transport firm; low F1 relevance; at most an option for corporate hospitality with transport and logistics customers at European races.

name: Haco
